## Context / Problem
Discovery (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md`) covers tests only as
smelly/missing tests (#7 `:51-52`; an `rg` count of files with <2 assertions,
`references/patterns.md:116-118`) and change-detector/duplication/dead-path health (#11 `:119-132`).
Neither asks: **can this assertion fail when the contract is violated?** No concern covers oracle
strength or contract-coverage gaps (a documented promise no test fails on). And
`phases/verification.md:115` anchors `prod_impact = none` at "docs/test-only", so a weak-test
finding sits below the impact floor and is dropped however critical the contract it fails to guard.
Six weak-oracle bugs escaped 7-21 Aug 2026 (e.g. `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`,
`9bb7-4430-1202-4d93`); no pre-bug janitor run would have surfaced any.

The rubric naming these classes ALREADY exists at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`
(`fail-open oracle` `:56-70`, `unrealistic fault injection` `:45-49`, ten false-positive guards
`:71-106`) but runs **only on a diff**, never on the resting tree: the gap is reach, not vocabulary.
Approved 2026-08-21. Testing philosophy: behavioural/contractual, not coverage.

## Approach
Add concern **#12 "Oracle strength and contract coverage"** to `phases/discovery.md`, sharded by
test-tree region as #11 is (`:131-132`) and cross-referenced from #11.

- **Brief.** Per test, name the contract under test (docstring, ADR, `--help` text, schema
  statement) and the oracle (its assertion set). Finding = the oracle cannot fail on a violation of
  that contract, proven by a concrete `escape_input` (a state the oracle accepts but the contract
  forbids). Same proof shape for contract-coverage gaps.
- **Cite `code-review-tests.md`; never restate it** — where it exists (a rebar checkout) it is the
  single source of truth. **Portable fallback (required — janitor also runs on repos lacking it):**
  `references/patterns.md` carries a portable core: the oracle-strength question, the `escape_input`
  requirement, the false-positive floor.
- **Already covered; #12 must NOT re-declare as new:** absent-string / empty-capture assertions with
  no producer-liveness check -> `fail-open oracle` `:56-70`; a race test whose primary
  synchronization is a timing sleep -> `:49`; every do-not-flag guard -> (ii)-(x) `:71-106`.
- **Do not flag:** apply guards (ii)-(x) (`code-review-tests.md:71-106`) by reference — mocks at
  external boundaries, exact-value asserts on pure functions, output greps with established producer
  liveness, Rule-5 structural greps, strict `xfail` with a named removal condition, secondary
  settling sleeps, bare "no test for X" with no violating input.
- **Additional instances** (verified absent from the rubric), named by #12: a fixture mutating
  state it did not create; an equivalence test whose two sides use different hardening helpers; an
  oracle encoding a policy preference the contract does not state.
- **Evidence shape.** New schema fields: `contract` (quote + `path:line`), `oracle` (quote +
  `path:line`), `escape_input`, `antipattern_id` (from `code-review-tests.md` where one applies,
  else the portable-core id), `scope` (sibling-site count). `discovery.md:152` — the schema handed
  to every discovery subagent — hardcodes "eleven concerns" -> "twelve".
- **Verification.** Amend `phases/verification.md:115` so a test-only finding takes `prod_impact`
  from the **production contract it fails to guard**, not from the file being under `tests/`.
  `harm_reachable` needs a tree-state demonstration (run against a deliberately broken stub, or
  reason the `escape_input` through the assertion); else the existing reclassification at
  `verification.md:49-50` applies — `HARDENING`, not `DEFECT`.
- **Feedback loop.** A #12 finding whose class the diff rubric lacks becomes a Phase-5 ticket
  adding it to `code-review-tests.md`.
- **Frontmatter constraint.** `SKILL.md`'s `description` enumerates the concerns and is **980 chars
  against the 1024 cap** (`scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`) — an oracle-strength mention must
  fit the 44 chars of headroom or displace wording.

## Scope
Under `examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/`: `phases/discovery.md` (#12, the #11 cross-reference,
schema fields, "eleven"->"twelve" at `:152`); `phases/verification.md` (`prod_impact` anchor `:115`);
`references/patterns.md` (portable core + #12 query); `SKILL.md` (frontmatter `description`, only if
it still fits under 1024 chars).

Not in scope: no `docs/` page documents the janitor concern list (verified by
`grep -rln "janitor" docs/`). `tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py` (the real skill-lint
test; `tests/unit/test_skill_frontmatter.py` does not exist) needs no edit — it tests the script,
not skill bodies. `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py:16-17` excludes rebar-janitor, so no
shared-copy sync applies.

## Testing
Documentation-only; no production code path changes. `check_skill_frontmatter.py` validates
only `**/SKILL.md` frontmatter, so it covers the `description` edit and nothing else; the phase- and
reference-file edits are proven by the greps below. `make lint` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
Commands run from the repo root after `J=examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor`.
- [ ] `discovery.md` carries #12 with its title: `grep -qE '^12\. \*\*Oracle strength and contract coverage\*\*' $J/phases/discovery.md` exits 0 (no `12.` line exists today).
- [ ] #12 requires an escape input and is sharded like #11: `awk '/^12\. \*\*Oracle strength/,/^### Temporal decay pass/' $J/phases/discovery.md | grep -qi "escape_input"` and the same range `| grep -qi "shard"` both exit 0.
- [ ] #12 cites the diff rubric rather than duplicating it: `awk '/^12\. \*\*Oracle strength/,/^### Temporal decay pass/' $J/phases/discovery.md | grep -q "code-review-tests.md"` exits 0, and the same range contains no re-declaration of the covered classes — `| grep -ciE "fail-open oracle|strict xfail|settling"` returns `0` (they are cited by reference only).
- [ ] The portable fallback exists in the skill tree: `grep -qi "oracle" $J/references/patterns.md` exits 0.
- [ ] The output schema gained the #12 fields: `for f in contract oracle escape_input antipattern_id scope; do grep -q "^- \`$f\`" $J/phases/discovery.md || { echo "MISSING $f"; exit 1; }; done` exits 0.
- [ ] The concern count is consistent: `grep -c "which of the eleven concerns above" $J/phases/discovery.md` returns `0` and `grep -q "which of the twelve concerns above" $J/phases/discovery.md` exits 0.
- [ ] #11 cross-references #12: `awk '/^11\. \*\*Test-suite health/,/^### Temporal decay pass/' $J/phases/discovery.md | grep -q "#12"` exits 0.
- [ ] `verification.md` no longer anchors `prod_impact` at "docs/test-only" unconditionally: `grep -n "none = docs/test-only" $J/phases/verification.md` returns a line that also names the guarded production contract, or returns nothing and `grep -qi "guarded production contract" $J/phases/verification.md` exits 0.
- [ ] `verification.md` requires a tree-state demonstration before a #12 finding can be `DEFECT`: `grep -qi "tree-state demonstration" $J/phases/verification.md` exits 0.
- [ ] Frontmatter still lints: `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` exits 0 and reports `PASS: 4 SKILL.md file(s)`.
- [ ] No collateral edits: `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only files named in Scope.
- [ ] Gates pass: `pytest tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q` and `make lint` exit 0.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Dry run on `git checkout 6fb4d801c9^` (`obvious-saline-gerbil` pre-fix tree) reports the fail-open absent-string oracle with a concrete `escape_input`; transcript posted as a comment. Non-gating: stochastic output, recorded for calibration.
